headline: Ratchet & Clank's source becomes easier to read while keeping its full code match
summary: Ratchet & Clank's decompiled source gained readable names, shared types and folders grouped by game system. All 5,116 functions remain matched: they compile to exactly the same bytes as the original game, with matched code by size at 100%. Data blocks and pointers also moved into C, using values generated from each contributor's own game copy.
highlights: #188, #189 and #190 replace button, level and hero-state numbers with names.
#171 removes 8,730 unused declarations; #172 consolidates shared function declarations into headers.
#196, #197 and #198 move data into C; the last batch reports compiled data reaching 74%.
#194 and #195 identify compiler workarounds and remove 48 that were unnecessary, preserving the match.
#204 adds checks that detect matching regressions, while #210 documents the reorganized source and remaining work.
